senses.definition: The narrow end or point of something.
senses.example: The tip of the pencil snapped.

senses.definition: A helpful piece of advice.
senses.example: Her best tip was to bring a map on the hike.

senses.definition: An extra amount of money given for a service.
senses.example: We left a tip for the server at the diner.

senses.definition: To lean, turn, or push something out of its upright position.
senses.example: Tip the bucket to pour the water into the drain.

senses.definition: To give someone a little extra money for a service.
senses.example: At the diner, they tipped the server after breakfast.

senses.definition: To walk quietly on the front parts of your feet.
senses.example: I tiptoed past the room where the baby was asleep.

senses.definition: A thick ring, often made partly of rubber and filled with air, that goes around the outside of a wheel.
senses.example: We checked the bicycle tire before leaving.

senses.definition: To make or become tired from work, movement, or worry.
senses.example: Climbing the long hill began to tire us.

senses.definition: Needing rest because you have used up much of your energy.
senses.example: I was too tired after the hike to finish the game.

senses.definition: Bored or annoyed from doing or hearing something too often.
senses.example: She was tired of reading the same story every night.

senses.definition: Past form of tire, meaning made or became tired.
senses.example: The long climb tired us out.

senses.definition: Body material made of a group of cells and nearby material working together.
senses.example: Muscle tissue can pull as it shortens.

senses.definition: A person or thing with great power, size, or importance.
senses.example: In the story, the enormous cedar was the titan of the forest.

senses.definition: The name of a book, song, article, or other work.
senses.example: I wrote the title at the top of my drawing.

senses.definition: A name or label that shows a person’s role, rank, or honor.
senses.example: Team captain is a title given to one player this season.

senses.definition: A kind of frog, often with short back legs and dry, bumpy skin.
senses.example: A small toad hid under the edge of the flowerpot.

senses.definition: Bread made brown and crisp by heat.
senses.example: I spread jam on a slice of toast.

senses.definition: Words spoken in someone’s honor, often before people lift a glass and drink.
senses.example: We made a toast to the winners with our cups of juice.

senses.definition: To brown or warm something with heat.
senses.example: We toasted the bread until both sides were golden.

senses.definition: On or during the day that is happening now.
senses.example: Our class is visiting the planetarium today.

senses.definition: The day that is happening now, or the present time.
senses.example: Today is the first day of our school break.

senses.definition: With each other in the same place, at the same time, or working as one group.
senses.example: We painted the two sides of the sign together.

senses.definition: Into one group or in contact with each other.
senses.example: Push the two blocks together until the gaps disappear.

senses.definition: To work very hard, often for a long time.
senses.example: The workers toiled through the afternoon to repair the footbridge.

senses.definition: A bowl with water, pipes, and usually a seat that people use to get rid of body waste.
senses.example: The plumber fixed the toilet so it would flush again.

senses.definition: A room containing a toilet, especially in British English.
senses.example: A sign in the station showed the way to the toilets.

senses.definition: Money paid to use something such as a road or bridge.
senses.example: The driver stopped to pay the bridge toll.

senses.definition: To ring a bell slowly, often one stroke at a time.
senses.example: We heard the tower bell toll each hour.

senses.definition: A soft, juicy fruit, usually red when ready to eat, that people often use like a vegetable.
senses.example: We cut a ripe tomato for the sandwiches.

senses.definition: On or during the day after today.
senses.example: I will finish the drawing tomorrow.

senses.definition: The day after today, or a time in the future.
senses.example: Tomorrow is the last day of the fair.

senses.definition: The soft part inside your mouth that helps you taste, speak, and move food.
senses.example: The sour candy made my tongue tingle.

senses.definition: A strip that sits between the laces and the top of a shoe.
senses.example: The tongue of my sneaker twisted while I tied it.

senses.definition: A language or way of speaking.
senses.example: They sang the song in their first tongue.

senses.definition: Something used to help do a job, such as a hammer, a pencil, or a computer program.
senses.example: The right tool helped us turn the small screw.

senses.definition: One of the hard parts in the mouth that help you bite and chew food.
senses.example: My loose tooth finally came out.

senses.definition: One of several little points that stick out in a row on something such as a comb or gear.
senses.example: A tooth broke off my comb.

senses.definition: A small brush used to clean teeth.
senses.example: I put a clean toothbrush in my overnight bag.

senses.definition: The highest part, surface, or point of something.
senses.example: We reached the top of the hill before lunch.

senses.definition: A piece that covers a container, or a piece of clothing worn above the waist.
senses.example: I put the top back on the jar.

senses.definition: To put something on the highest part of something else, or to be greater than something.
senses.example: We topped each muffin with one blueberry.

senses.definition: A subject people are talking, writing, or learning about.
senses.example: Our topic this week is how bridges hold weight.

senses.definition: A map that shows the shapes and heights of the land, along with places and features on it.
senses.example: The walkers used a topographic map to find the steepest hill.

senses.definition: To fall over from an upright position or make something do that.
senses.example: One little bump made the pile of blocks topple.

senses.definition: A stick with a flame at one end used for light, or a small handheld electric light in British English.
senses.example: In the play, a paper torch lit the pretend castle hall.

senses.definition: A violently spinning column of air that reaches from a storm cloud to the ground.
senses.example: We read a story about a town after a tornado.

senses.definition: A kind of turtle that lives mostly on land and often has a high, rounded shell.
senses.example: The tortoise moved slowly across the sandy ground.

senses.definition: To throw something lightly or carelessly.
senses.example: Please toss the ball back to me.

senses.definition: To mix food by moving the pieces lightly about.
senses.example: We tossed the lettuce and tomatoes in a big bowl.

senses.definition: A throw, often a light one or a flip of a coin.
senses.example: A coin toss decided who would play first.

senses.definition: The whole amount after parts are added together.
senses.example: The total of my two scores was fourteen.

senses.definition: Including all of something, or complete.
senses.example: Our total time on the trail was two hours.

senses.definition: To add amounts together or come to a certain amount when added.
senses.example: The five piles total thirty cards.

senses.definition: To put a part of yourself against something or come into contact with it.
senses.example: Do not touch the picture until the paint is dry.

senses.definition: To make someone feel a strong emotion, often a warm or sad one.
senses.example: Their kind letter touched me.

senses.definition: The sense that lets you feel something when it makes contact with your body.
senses.example: By touch alone, I could tell which block had a rough edge.

senses.definition: Hard to break, cut, or wear out.
senses.example: We used tough fabric to patch the bag.

senses.definition: Difficult or demanding.
senses.example: The last question on the quiz was tough.

senses.definition: Able to face trouble or pain without giving up easily.
senses.example: She stayed tough during a long, tiring hike.

senses.definition: A trip through a place or several places to look around or learn.
senses.example: We took a tour of the puppet workshop.

senses.definition: To visit parts of a place or several places to look around, teach, or perform.
senses.example: The band will tour small towns this summer.

senses.definition: A series of games or matches used to decide an overall winner.
senses.example: Our chess tournament lasted three afternoons.

senses.definition: To pull a vehicle, boat, or trailer along behind.
senses.example: A small boat towed the raft back to the dock.

senses.definition: In the direction of someone or something, or in a way that helps reach a goal.
senses.example: We followed the path toward the orchard.

senses.definition: A piece of cloth or paper used for drying or wiping things.
senses.example: I used a towel to dry my hands.

senses.definition: To dry something by rubbing it with a towel.
senses.example: I toweled my hair before getting on the bus.

senses.definition: A tall, narrow building or structure, often standing by itself or attached to a larger building.
senses.example: A stone tower stood at one end of the old wall.

senses.definition: To stand much higher than other things nearby.
senses.example: Tall pines towered over our tent.

senses.definition: A place where people live and work close together, often larger than a village and smaller than a city.
senses.example: Our town has a library next to the little park.

senses.definition: A building used for local government or a public meeting for people to discuss issues.
senses.example: We went to town hall to see the old photographs on display.

senses.definition: An object made for children to play with or an object used mainly for fun.
senses.example: We took a small toy on the long train ride.

senses.definition: To think briefly about an idea without deciding on it, usually followed by with.
senses.example: We toyed with the idea of making the sign in the shape of a turtle.

senses.definition: A very small amount, or a mark left as a sign of something.
senses.example: We could see a trace of blue paint on the handle.

senses.definition: To copy a shape by following its lines, often through thin paper.
senses.example: I traced a leaf before adding its tiny veins.

senses.definition: To follow tracks, clues, or a line to find where something goes or began.
senses.example: We traced the creek on the map to find the pond.

senses.definition: A preserved sign of what a living thing did long ago, such as a track or burrow.
senses.example: The track in the rock is a trace fossil of a dinosaur walking.

senses.definition: A path or set of rails that guides movement.
senses.example: The two tracks ran side by side through the town.

senses.definition: A mark left by a foot, wheel, or other moving thing.
senses.example: A small track in the snow led to the hedge.

senses.definition: One song or piece of sound saved as part of a recording.
senses.example: My favorite track is the last song on the album.

senses.definition: To follow where something moves, or keep a record of it over time.
senses.example: We tracked how far the caterpillar crawled each minute.

senses.definition: A strong motor vehicle used to pull or operate farm equipment and other heavy loads.
senses.example: The tractor pulled a trailer full of pumpkins.

senses.definition: To give something to someone and receive something else in return.
senses.example: I will trade a blue bead for a red one.

senses.definition: The buying, selling, or exchanging of goods and services.
senses.example: Trade brings some fruits from warm places to places where they cannot grow.

senses.definition: Work that uses a particular skill people can learn, such as fixing pipes or making furniture.
senses.example: It takes training and practice to learn the carpenter’s trade.

senses.definition: Vehicles or people moving along a route, or the amount of movement there.
senses.example: Traffic slowed when a lane was closed.

senses.definition: The amount of activity on a network or website.
senses.example: The site had more traffic when the new game came out.

senses.definition: A path through an area, often made or marked for people to follow.
senses.example: The trail led past a stream and into the woods.

senses.definition: A line of marks left behind as someone or something moves.
senses.example: The muddy boots left a trail across the porch.

senses.definition: To follow or hang behind something as it moves.
senses.example: The scarf trailed behind her in the wind.

senses.definition: One or more vehicles that run on railway tracks together to carry people or goods.
senses.example: We watched a long freight train cross the bridge.

senses.definition: To practice or teach a skill so someone gets better at it.
senses.example: Our neighbor trains dogs to guide people safely.

senses.definition: A feature of a living thing that can be noticed or measured.
senses.example: The color of a flower is a trait.

senses.definition: To step heavily on something and damage or flatten it.
senses.example: People used the marked path so they would not trample the flowers.

senses.definition: A piece of equipment with a tight, stretchy surface on a frame that people can bounce on.
senses.example: We took turns bouncing in the middle of the trampoline.

senses.definition: To move or pass someone or something from one place, group, or person to another.
senses.example: We transferred the seedlings into bigger pots.

senses.definition: An act of moving from one thing to another, such as changing buses to reach a place.
senses.example: Our bus route needed one transfer.

senses.definition: A device that uses a changing magnetic field between coils of wire to change electric voltage.
senses.example: The transformer lowers the voltage for use in the building.

senses.definition: To use another language to say or write what words in one language mean.
senses.example: Our neighbor translated the note into Spanish.

senses.definition: To turn something into a different form.
senses.example: The map translated the size of the whole park into a drawing we could hold.

senses.definition: The release of water vapor from a plant, mostly through its leaves.
senses.example: Transpiration added water vapor to the air around the tree.

senses.definition: A device or situation that catches or holds someone or something.
senses.example: A wildlife worker checked the trap used to catch and move the animal.

senses.definition: To catch or hold something so it cannot easily get away.
senses.example: The thick blanket traps warm air near your body.

senses.definition: A flat shape with four straight sides and at least one pair of opposite sides that are parallel. Some schoolbooks use the name only when there is exactly one such pair.
senses.example: The trapezoid I drew had a short top edge parallel to its longer bottom edge.

senses.definition: Things that people throw away because they do not want or need them.
senses.example: We picked up trash around the playground.

senses.definition: To damage or make a big mess of something, or to throw it away.
senses.example: The storm trashed the cardboard sign we left outside.

senses.definition: To go from one place to another.
senses.example: We traveled by bus through three towns.

senses.definition: To move or spread from one place to another, as sound, light, or news can do.
senses.example: Sound can travel through the air from one room to another.

senses.definition: A flat object with a small rim used to carry or hold things.
senses.example: We carried the cups on a tray so they would not fall.

senses.definition: Something very valuable or dear to someone, or a collection of such things.
senses.example: Old photos were the greatest treasure in the box.

senses.definition: To care about something very much and want to keep it.
senses.example: I treasure the notebook my friend made for me.

senses.definition: To act toward someone or handle something in a certain way.
senses.example: Please treat the library books with care.

senses.definition: To give medical care for an illness or injury.
senses.example: The nurse helped treat the skater’s scraped knee.

senses.definition: Something special that is given or enjoyed.
senses.example: We had fresh berries as a treat after dinner.

senses.definition: A formal agreement between countries or other governments.
senses.example: The two countries signed a treaty to settle their disagreement about fishing rights.

senses.definition: A tall plant that usually has one hard, thick main stem and branches above the ground.
senses.example: A tree shaded the yard in the afternoon.

senses.definition: An opening inside the trunk or a branch of a tree.
senses.example: A house wren can take small sticks into a tree cavity for a nest.

senses.definition: A frame that a climbing plant can grow on.
senses.example: Pea plants climbed the trellis by the fence.

senses.definition: To shake slightly, often because of cold, excitement, or fear.
senses.example: My hands began to tremble when I stepped onto the stage.

senses.definition: Very large, strong, or impressive.
senses.example: The crowd made a tremendous noise when play began.

senses.definition: A direction in which things are generally changing, or a style becoming popular.
senses.example: We noticed a trend toward warmer days in our class weather chart.

senses.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides and three corners.
senses.example: We cut a triangle from the corner of the paper.

senses.definition: A stream or river that flows into another stream or river.
senses.example: The creek is a tributary of the larger river downstream.

senses.definition: A muscle at the back of your upper arm that helps straighten your elbow.
senses.example: Your triceps muscle works when you push your hand away from your shoulder.

senses.definition: Something done to fool someone or a clever action done for fun.
senses.example: The magician’s trick made a coin seem to vanish.

senses.definition: A clever way to do something easily.
senses.example: Grandpa showed me a trick for folding a map.

senses.definition: To cause someone to believe something false or do something they did not mean to do.
senses.example: The costume tricked me into thinking a bear was at the gate.

senses.definition: To flow or come a little at a time.
senses.example: Water trickled down the stone wall after the rain.

senses.definition: A thin flow, or a small number of things arriving slowly.
senses.example: Only a trickle of water came from the end of the hose.

senses.definition: To cut off extra bits or make something neat by cutting.
senses.example: We trimmed the paper to fit the frame.

senses.definition: A strip or decoration around the edge of something.
senses.example: The blue coat had bright red trim.

senses.definition: Neat and in good order.
senses.example: The front yard looked trim after we cut the grass.

senses.definition: A group of three people or things, especially three people making music.
senses.example: A trio of students played the tune on their recorders.

senses.definition: A journey from one place to another and often back again.
senses.example: We took a trip to visit the old lighthouse.

senses.definition: To catch your foot on something and lose your balance, or to cause someone to do this.
senses.example: I tripped over the rug but stayed on my feet.

senses.definition: A success that feels especially important after effort or difficulty.
senses.example: Finishing the long puzzle together felt like a triumph.

senses.definition: To succeed or win after doing something difficult.
senses.example: The smallest team triumphed in the final match.

senses.definition: An object given as a prize for winning or doing especially well.
senses.example: Our team shared the trophy with the coach.

senses.definition: A warm, very wet forest that grows in the tropics.
senses.example: The tall trees in the tropical rain forest stayed green through the year.

senses.definition: To move at a steady pace faster than a walk and slower than a fast run.
senses.example: The pony trotted down the path beside us.

senses.definition: A problem, difficulty, or situation that causes worry.
senses.example: We had trouble reading the map in the dark.

senses.definition: To worry, bother, or cause problems for someone.
senses.example: One unanswered question still troubled me.

senses.definition: One of several fish from the salmon family, many of which live in cool freshwater.
senses.example: We saw a trout holding still beneath the stream’s surface.

senses.definition: A motor vehicle made to carry loads, often with a large open or closed space behind the driver.
senses.example: A truck delivered a pile of boards to the school.

senses.definition: To move something by truck.
senses.example: They trucked the heavy equipment to the new building.

senses.definition: A brass instrument played by blowing with vibrating lips into a small mouthpiece.
senses.example: I heard a trumpet before the band turned the corner.

senses.definition: To make a loud sound like a trumpet or announce something very proudly.
senses.example: The elephant trumpeted when the other elephants came near.

senses.definition: The main hard stem of a tree from which the branches grow.
senses.example: We measured how far around the tree trunk was.

senses.definition: The long flexible nose of an elephant.
senses.example: The elephant used its trunk to lift a branch.

senses.definition: A space for carrying things in a car, or a large box used to store or carry things.
senses.example: We loaded the suitcase into the trunk of the car.

senses.definition: To believe someone will act honestly or dependably, or that something will work as expected.
senses.example: I trusted my friend to bring back the book.

senses.definition: A belief that someone or something will be honest, safe, or dependable.
senses.example: Our group built trust by keeping its promises.

senses.definition: What is true or what actually happened.
senses.example: The truth was that we had both reached for the same pen.

senses.definition: A chart that lists the result of a logic rule for each possible set of true and false choices.
senses.example: The truth table shows when the alarm button should turn on a sign.

senses.definition: To make an effort to do something.
senses.example: I tried to count the stars but kept losing my place.

senses.definition: To test, taste, or use something to find out what it is like.
senses.example: Would you like to try a slice of pear?

senses.definition: An attempt at doing something.
senses.example: I caught the ball on my second try.

senses.definition: To test something new and see how well it works or how you like it.
senses.example: Can we try out the new track before the race?

senses.definition: To show what you can do in hopes of being chosen for a group or role.
senses.example: I’m going to try out for a part in the school play.

senses.definition: A deep, open container, often used for water, washing, or storing food.
senses.example: I put the wet brushes in a tub beside the sink.

senses.definition: A long hollow object that can carry something through it or hold something inside it.
senses.example: The marble rolled through a cardboard tube.

senses.definition: The soft, movable parts that a sea star and some related animals use to move or handle food.
senses.example: The sea star gripped a rock with dozens of tube feet.

senses.definition: A swollen part of a plant that stores food and can grow new shoots in some plants.
senses.example: A potato is a tuber on an underground stem.

senses.definition: To push, fold, or place something neatly into a small or protected spot.
senses.example: I tucked the note into the side pocket.

senses.definition: To pull sharply or firmly.
senses.example: I tugged the rope to ring the bell.

senses.definition: A quick pull, or a strong little boat that helps move larger ships.
senses.example: We watched a tug guide a big ship past the pier.

senses.definition: A plant that grows from a bulb and usually has a bright, cup-shaped flower.
senses.example: The first red tulip opened beside the porch.

senses.definition: To fall, roll, or move over and over without staying balanced.
senses.example: The blocks tumbled off the table.

senses.definition: A fall in which someone or something turns or rolls.
senses.example: My hat took a tumble down the steps.

senses.definition: A series of musical notes that you can recognize as a whole.
senses.example: I hummed the tune as we walked home.

senses.definition: To adjust an instrument so it plays the right pitches, or adjust a device so it works well.
senses.example: The band tuned its instruments before the show.

senses.definition: A two-pronged metal tool that vibrates at a steady rate to give a reference note.
senses.example: The teacher tapped a tuning fork before the choir began.

senses.definition: A long passage running through or under earth, rock, water, or a structure.
senses.example: The train went into a tunnel and came out near the river.

senses.definition: To dig or make a passage through something.
senses.example: The rabbit tunneled through soft soil under the fence.

senses.definition: A wheel with blades that spins when flowing water, air or steam pushes on it.
senses.example: Moving water turned a turbine inside the dam.

senses.definition: To move around a point, change direction, or make something face a new way.
senses.example: Turn the knob toward the red mark.

senses.definition: To change into a different state or condition.
senses.example: Some leaves turn yellow in autumn.

senses.definition: A person’s chance to do something in order with others.
senses.example: It is your turn to roll the dice.

senses.definition: To make the level or strength of something higher.
senses.example: Can you turn up the sound a little?

senses.definition: To appear or be found, often after people stopped expecting it.
senses.example: My other glove may turn up in the lost and found.

senses.definition: A round root vegetable that is often white with purple near the top.
senses.example: Mom chopped a turnip to add to the soup.

senses.definition: A reptile with a protective shell around much of its body. Some kinds live in water and others live mostly on land.
senses.example: A turtle warmed itself on a log above the water.

senses.definition: A long tooth that sticks out past an animal’s mouth.
senses.example: A narwhal’s tusk is a long tooth that sticks out from its upper jaw.

senses.definition: A special suit worn for formal events, often dark with shiny lapels.
senses.example: The band leader wore a tuxedo for the evening concert.

senses.definition: A small thin branch, often one that has fallen from a tree or bush.
senses.example: I drew circles in the sand with a twig.

senses.definition: One of two children born from the same pregnancy.
senses.example: My neighbor’s twin lives across town.

senses.definition: Made up of two things that match, look alike, or come as a pair.
senses.example: The toy boat had twin sails.

senses.definition: A light cord made by twisting several strings together.
senses.example: We tied the bundle of sticks with twine.

senses.definition: To twist or wind one thing around another.
senses.example: Bean stems twined around the narrow poles.

senses.definition: To shine with small changing flashes of light, or to seem to do so.
senses.example: The stars twinkled above the dark field.

senses.definition: A small changing light or a bright, playful look in someone’s eyes.
senses.example: A twinkle in his eyes told me he was joking.

senses.definition: To turn one end of something while holding the other, or bend something into a winding shape.
senses.example: Twist the two ends of the paper together.

senses.definition: An unexpected change in a story or plan.
senses.example: There was a twist at the end of the chapter.

senses.definition: A way to sign in that checks two different kinds of proof that you are allowed to use the account.
senses.example: My family turned on two-factor authentication for an account.

senses.definition: A kind or group of things with shared features.
senses.example: This type of bag is made for carrying books.

senses.definition: To enter letters, numbers, or other symbols using a keyboard.
senses.example: I typed the names into a list.

senses.definition: A preserved example linked to the scientific name of a group of living things, often a species.
senses.example: A scientist compared the plant to the type specimen kept in a herbarium.

senses.definition: Showing what often happens or what most things of a certain kind are like.
senses.example: A typical day at camp starts with breakfast and a short walk.

senses.definition: Someone who types words on a keyboard, especially as part of a job.
senses.example: The typist entered the names from the handwritten list.
